records.title: feat(scan): follow local uses: edges into composite actions so nested references are managed
records.body:
## Context

`gx` discovers action references at depth 1. The scanner reads `.github/workflows/*.{yml,yaml}`, walks `jobs[].steps[].uses`, and drops any reference beginning with `.` (`src/infra/workflow_scan/scanner.rs:176`):

```rust
if action_name.starts_with('.') || action_name.starts_with("docker://") {
    continue;
}
```

But a local `uses:` is not a dependency to skip — it is an **edge into more of this repo's own action tree**.

## The gap

Given:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
- uses: ./.github/actions/build        # dropped at scanner.rs:176
```
```yaml
# .github/actions/build/action.yml
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4        # never discovered
```

`gx lint` reports the repo **clean**, `gx tidy` leaves the action **unpinned**, and `gx.lock` **omits** it.

An unpinned action inside a repo's own composite is exactly the supply-chain exposure `gx` exists to close — the tag can be moved to point at different code, and the pin that would prevent it is never written. This is a security-visibility gap, not a convenience gap.

## Proposal

Turn the local-edge drop into a resolve-and-recurse:

1. A local `uses:` (`./path`) resolves against the repo root to `path/action.yml` or `path/action.yaml`.
2. That file is parsed (needs #123) and its `uses:` references are extracted.
3. **Remote** references found at any depth become first-class `Located` entries, identical to depth-1 ones.
4. **Local** references found there are followed in turn — fully recursive.
5. A visited-set of canonical paths terminates cycles.

### Traversal rule

- **Local edges are followed, never recorded.** `./.github/actions/build` has no version and no SHA; it is this repo. It is a path to more nodes, not a lock entry.
- **Remote edges terminate the walk and are recorded.** `gx` does **not** fetch a remote action's `action.yml` to walk its subtree — pinning that action's SHA already freezes it transitively.
- The repo boundary is the traversal boundary.

```
ci.yml
 └─ ./.github/actions/build      (followed)
     ├─ actions/checkout@v4      → managed
     └─ ./.github/actions/setup  (followed)
         └─ actions/cache@v4     → managed
```

## Invariants

- Lock entries stay keyed on **remote identity**. The same `actions/checkout@v4` used in a workflow and in a composite is one managed entry observed at two locations — already modelled by `Located`/`Location`.
- Cycles terminate; a self-referencing or mutually-referencing composite must not hang or overflow.
- A local edge whose target is missing is handled in a follow-up lint rule; it must not panic here.

## Rollout

**On by default.** Repos with unpinned actions inside composites will newly fail `gx lint` — that is the intended effect, and it is a real finding, not a false positive. Worth a CHANGELOG note.

## Non-goals

- `docker://` references stay filtered — a different identity kind needing a registry client, out of scope for reachable-tree work.
- No new discovery roots; the root set stays `.github/workflows/*.{yml,yaml}` (see #108 for the roots question).
- Job-level `uses:` is tracked separately.

## Depends on

- **#123** — composite-action model. Nothing to traverse into until `action.yml` can be parsed.
- **#126** — `Location`/`ActionOverride` addressing. Must be **decided** first: this issue changes what `gx tidy` writes into users' `gx.toml`, and under the current model a nested reference (`job: None, step: None`) makes `overrides::sync` either drop existing overrides or collapse every composite's actions into one slot. The traversal logic here is unaffected — only what gets recorded downstream.

Spine order: #123 → #126 → #124.

records.title: hull: generic subtree-aggregation service over the containment tree (the design suite's critical path)
records.body:
**In plain terms:** Add a read-only service that, for any node in the asset registry's containment
tree, computes a rolled-up metric over everything beneath it (e.g. "how many rooms are inside this
building", "average condition of all equipment under this floor") plus the same number broken down
per direct child — so the design suite's KPI cards can show "any node rolls up what's beneath it."

**Why it matters:** 7 of 16 design-suite prototypes compute live descendant rollups (counts, sums,
averages, ratios). Today the registry can only read a node's DIRECT contents — there is no
subtree/descendant read at all, and no aggregation. This is the design suite's critical-path
substrate (pack-over-pillars ruling, decision-log 2026-07-22).

**Done when:** `GET {AssetRegistryRoutes.RouteBase}/entities/{id}/rollup` returns, for a metric
spec, the subtree aggregate over a node's transitive containment descendants (as-of clock) plus a
direct-children breakdown — computed on the in-memory registry stores the node host already wires,
and covered by a mutation-proof test on a realistic multi-level fixture.

---
**Technical detail (for agents):**

**CORRECTED PREMISE — the original card named the wrong substrate. Ground these on `origin/main`
before writing a line.** The original body said "foundation-assets-postgres + AssetRegistryRoutes +
a single recursive CTE." All three are false:

1. **`AssetRegistryRoutes` is NOT backed by foundation-assets-postgres.** It is backed by the
   **in-memory Rev-3 registry stores** — `IRegistryEntityRepository` / `ITypedRelationshipStore` /
   `IConditionAssessmentStore` from `packages/blocks-assets-registry`
   (`Services/InMemoryRegistryEntityRepository.cs`, `Services/InMemoryTypedRelationshipStore.cs`).
   The node host wires them at
   `apps/local-node-host/Data/AssetRegistry/NodeAssetRegistryComposition.cs:51`
   (`.AddInMemoryAssetTypeSystem()`). No persistence-backed registry backend exists anywhere.
2. **`foundation-assets-postgres` is a DISJOINT, frozen model.** It implements a different contract
   set (`IEntityStore` / `IHierarchyService` keyed off the `EntityId` scheme/authority/local-part
   triple, over a materialized closure table — `packages/foundation-assets-postgres/Hierarchy/ClosureRow.cs`),
   and is referenced ONLY by test projects of `blocks-property-equipment` / `blocks-properties` /
   `blocks-businesscases` / `blocks-subscriptions` (the Rev-2 concrete Asset/Equipment domain,
   **frozen** pending the promotion wave — `packages/blocks-assets-registry/README.md` lines 8-9).
   `apps/local-node-host` never references it.
3. **"Single recursive CTE" is wrong on both models.** The registry store is in-memory (no SQL).
   Even the postgres closure model reads a subtree with a plain indexed JOIN / range-scan over the
   pre-materialized closure table, NOT a recursive CTE (`PostgresHierarchyService.GetSubtreeAsync`,
   lines 337-357).

**Correct target (architectural determination, Admiral re-authoring 2026-07-24):** build the
aggregation on the **registry contracts** in `packages/blocks-assets-registry`, as a **query-layer
read model (ADR 0146 D4** — dataset rollups live in the query/read layer, never the rule-engine core
`agg`). The **only** implementation is **in-memory**, matching the stores the node host uses. Do
**not** touch `foundation-assets-postgres` — it is the wrong (disjoint, frozen) model and needs no
wiring. This is explicitly **not** a "wire postgres first" task; there is **no predecessor card**
(that false-premise reading is what got this card held).

**The subtree-descendant primitive is NEW.** `ITypedRelationshipStore` today exposes only DIRECT
contents (`GetContentsAsAtAsync`) + the upward path (`GetContainmentPathAsAtAsync`). Add the
transitive descendant walk: given `(tenant, root, asOf)`, the set of entities reachable via effective
`Contains` edges at `asOf`. Implement as a bounded BFS/DFS over the effective-Contains graph — reuse
the pattern already in `InMemoryTypedRelationshipStore` (`EffectiveContains`, `IsDescendant`,
`LongestChain`, `MaxContainmentDepth` default 32 + cycle-guard, lines 203-300). No N+1: the store
holds every edge in memory; one pass builds the child adjacency, one walk yields the subtree. Keep
the as-of-clock discipline (A5c) — every read takes an explicit `Instant`, never ambient now.

**The aggregation service.** Add `ISubtreeAggregationService` (+ in-memory impl) to
`blocks-assets-registry`. Contract:
`(TenantId, RegistryEntityId root, MetricSpec, Instant asOf) -> RollupResult { decimal? Aggregate,
IReadOnlyList<ChildBreakdown> Children }`, where each `ChildBreakdown` is
`(direct-child id, that child's own subtree aggregate)`. Metric-spec kinds:
- **`count`** — number of subtree descendants whose `Type` is in a caller-supplied set of
  `EntityTypeId`s.
- **`sum` / `avg`** — over a **value-resolver** applied to each subtree descendant. Ship exactly two
  built-in resolvers, both grounded in stores already injected into `As
